verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's documented programmatic lifecycle works at the cluster and Node Pool level, not per instance. Clusters can be created and deleted through the CKS API and Terraform, and Node Pools (groups of instances) scale through the Cluster Autoscaler. Spot and On-Demand capacity is described as pay-as-you-go. The docs never describe per-instance stop, start, or restart, or that stopped resources stop billing. Missing for 10: per-instance start/stop/restart operations, explicit per-instance terminate API, documentation that billing stops when nodes are removed or stopped, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can start, stop, restart, and terminate instances programmatically and keep paying only for what is running

citations.quote: The API lets you create, list, update, and delete managed Kubernetes clusters on CoreWeave infrastructure.
A Node Pool in CKS represents one or more instances that share a common configuration
CKS supports scaling Node Pools by using the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler, letting you scale CKS Node Pools in response to workload demands for GPU, CPU, or memory resources.
The CoreWeave Terraform provider lets you manage CoreWeave infrastructure as code, including CKS clusters
Spot Node Pools provide pay-as-you-go access to high-performance bare-metal compute resources without long-term commitments or reservations.
